signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Sanctions Escalation
signals.text: USD ranks as the strongest currency in the G10 strength scorecard with a 1W average gain of +1.151% across 9 pairs, while SEK sits as the weakest currency at -0.875% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme 2.026% bilateral spread. DXY trades above its SMA20, 50, and 200 cluster at 100.22, whereas USD/SEK spot at 9.826 trades comfortably above its own moving average suite (SMA20 9.631, SMA50 9.602). This performance gap is reinforced by newly signed Russia sanctions opening secondary tariff risks for China and India, compounding pressure on open-economy, export-sensitive currencies like SEK. Monetary policy divergence amplifies the move, with the Fed hiking to 4.00% versus the Riksbank on hold at 1.75%, establishing a 225bp nominal policy rate buffer and a +1.91% real rate wedge in favor of the dollar. The Swedish ESI sits deeply negative at -29.2, underscoring persistent domestic economic misses relative to stable US prints. Trade bias: Bullish USD/SEK, bilateral theme reinforced by widening macro fundamentals. Catalyst: Riksbank meeting 24 Sep — hold bias priced. Risk: Riksbank executes a surprise 25bp hike or tariff rhetoric decompresses, narrowing the bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Persistence vs Intervention Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.00, holding above its SMA20 of 156.79 while remaining capped below the SMA50/200 cluster at 159.05/158.40. A 275bp Fed-BoJ policy rate spread and a +287bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential continue to anchor spot demand despite the Bank of Japan raising its policy rate to 1.25%. Options markets display pronounced asymmetric defense against upside extension, evidenced by 25d risk reversals printing at -1.88 alongside an ATM implied volatility of 8.0% against an HV30 of 9.9%, generating a negative volatility risk premium of -1.9%. CFTC data reveals leveraged funds swinging sharply net long JPY to +20,069 contracts (pctl 95, z +1.57) following a weekly delta of +73,324, representing speculative positioning crowded into the upper decile of its 52-week range. With VIX contained at 14.8, broad safe-haven flows are absent, leaving the pair dictated by carry stability versus positioning unwind risk as price nears historical intervention sensitivity levels toward 160.00. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY, carry support constrained by heavy downside options hedging and spec crowding. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 30 Oct — hold stance expected. Risk: Verbal intervention escalates or spot drops below SMA20 at 156.79, initiating leveraged long unwinds.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning Friction
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7127, resting below its falling SMA20 at 0.7168 while supported above the SMA50 and SMA200 at 0.7087 and 0.7015. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds holding +59,299 net long contracts, placing institutional exposure at the 97th percentile of its 52-week range (z +2.11) after adding +10,920 contracts WoW. The RBA at 4.35% maintains a 35bp carry advantage over the Fed at 4.00% (AONIA-SOFR spread favors AUD by 50bp), yet spot momentum has stalled against fresh US tariff threats against Asian trade partners. ATM implied volatility runs at 6.5% against an HV30 of 5.5% (VRP +1.0%), while the 25d risk reversal reflects a mild put skew of -0.66, indicating options dealers are paying for downside hedges despite the institutional net long. Heavy speculative crowding leaves the currency vulnerable to sharp positioning flushes if risk appetite deteriorates. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, crowded long overhang limits upside follow-through. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold widely expected. Risk: Sustained daily close above SMA20 at 0.7168 accompanied by renewed commodity inflows.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Bearish Moving Average Alignment + Carry Deficit
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1485, pinned beneath its descending SMA20 at 1.1597, SMA50 at 1.1540, and SMA200 at 1.1633. The Fed's policy rate of 4.00% versus the ECB at 2.65% enforces a 135bp nominal policy differential, reflected in a +141bp SOFR-€STR OIS advantage favoring the dollar and maintaining structural downward drag on the pair. Leveraged funds remain net short EUR by -51,355 contracts (pctl 32, z -0.36) following a WoW expansion of -4,974 contracts, confirming institutional alignment with the rate deficit. While ECB rhetoric leaves the door open to a further hike should energy pressures mount, European real yields (+0.30%) lag US real rates (+1.59%) by 129bp, preventing capital attraction. Implied volatility sits at 4.5% versus HV30 of 4.2% with 25d risk reversals flat at -0.14, demonstrating an orderly grind lower rather than a disorderly unwind. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, moving average stack and carry deficit cap recovery attempts. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech 21 Sep at 11:00 UTC. Risk: Hawkish forward guidance from Lagarde pushes EUR/USD through SMA50 resistance at 1.1540.
